transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-10
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood CSM), Ethan (Northstar Head of ML), Priya (VP Eng), Sara (Procurement), David (Infra)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time, this is a renewal and expansion check-in, mostly to talk through Dedicated capacity options and the regions you asked about. quick intro round?
[00:12] Priya: Hi I'm Priya, VP Eng at Northstar — leading the infra expansion efforts.
[00:16] Ethan: Ethan here, head of ML, I'll be running the benchmarks and validating quality.
[00:20] Sara: Sara in procurement, I'll handle the contract side.
[00:24] David: David, infra lead, I'll coordinate networking.
[00:27] Maya: Maya from Redwood SE, I'll take the technical bits.
[00:30] Jordan: Great. Quick recap — on your current hosted plan you've been at about 25M tokens/month, burst to 45M last quarter, and the main ask was predictable throughput plus lower p99 latency for inference in EU and APAC, right?
[00:43] Ethan: Yeah that's right. We saw variance during peak routing and the caching didn't help as much for some conversational flows.
[00:50] David: Also want VPC connectivity in EU region with KMS integration.
[00:55] Jordan: Understood. So we recommended Dedicated pools with a baseline throughput of X tokens/sec, autoscale policies and optional burst capacity. today we'd like to walk through pricing options and a plan for adding EU and APAC regions.
[01:10] Priya: Quick question on latency — our SLO is 150ms p95 for the 1k token prompts. Bedrock was quoting similar but it's unclear about consistent tail latencies. how does Redwood guarantee tail behavior?
[01:26] Maya: Yeah big question. So we do a couple things — continuous batching tuned to your request size, KV cache for prefix-heavy flows, and kernel selection per model to avoid long-run slower ops. In Dedicated we can pin model variants and isolate the pool so you get predictable p95/p99. There is still variability due to, uh, network hops, but we've seen stable p95 under 120ms in our EU clusters in our internal tests.
[01:47] Ethan: When you say internal tests, can we run the same script against our data? we need apples-to-apples.
[01:52] Maya: Absolutely. We'll run the benchmark with your traffic profile. I'll send the script and a test plan; we can coordinate a VPC peering so the traffic path matches production.
[02:00] Jordan: We'll put the benchmark run on the calendar.
[02:04] Sara: On procurement, we need the contract lengths and options — 12 vs 24 month commit, breakpoints for adding capacity mid-term, and an estimate for extra regions. also SOC2 and data processing addendum.
[02:18] Jordan: For sure. We'll include a pricing spreadsheet with 12/24 month options and a separate line for regional add-ons and burst capacity. Liam will attach SOC2 and network diagrams.
[02:27] Liam: I'll share SOC2 report, network architecture diagram, and KMS integration notes after this call. expect a secure link.
[02:34] Priya: Another question — we have some regulatory customers in EU who require data residency; does Redwood Dedicated allow for data to remain in customer VPC in EU?
[02:44] Maya: With Dedicated we offer private deployment options — VPC peering into our EU region or if you need full isolation we have the Private deployment package, which is an on-prem or VPC-managed control plane. For many customers, VPC peering plus KMS meets residency + encryption requirements.
[02:58] David: For peering, what's the expected IP/Egress setup? we need ranges for firewall rules.
[03:03] Maya: We'll send the peering IP ranges in the network doc; staging will have temporary ranges.
[03:09] Ethan: About model variants — we currently use a 70B open model. Do you support quantized variants for throughput gains? will that change outputs significantly?
[03:20] Maya: We support INT8 quantized variants and some 4-bit paths depending on model. For the 70B it can reduce cost per token by ~35-50% with minimal quality delta for many tasks, but we'll want to run a quality regression on your eval prompts.
[03:33] Ethan: Ok let's add that to the benchmark.
[03:36] Jordan: pricing note — quantization options will be in the recommendation sheet so you can see cost vs quality tradeoffs.
[03:42] Priya: And SLOs for multi-region? If we add EU and APAC, is the routing automatic or do we manage region pins?
[03:50] Maya: Routing can be policy driven — latency-first will route to closest region, cost-first to cheaper pools, or you can pin a customer to EU-only pools. For regulatory customers you can pin at the route level.
[04:02] Sara: Any change to logging/audit access for Dedicated? our security team needs exportable audit logs.
[04:09] Liam: Dedicated includes audit logs with retention options; for Private deployments we can offer longer retention and custom export. I'll include examples in the docs.
[04:18] David: Can you provide an example of cost delta for adding APAC? we have a lot of traffic from APAC now.
[04:23] Jordan: We'll model that in the spreadsheet — estimate throughput and used tokens, then show Dedicated vs Hosted incremental. expect the spreadsheet by Thursday.
[04:32] Ethan: timeline wise — we want to finalize commitment by end of month if possible; procurement window is tight.
[04:37] Sara: Yes end of month would be ideal.
[04:40] Jordan: Great. so immediate deliverables: quote + SOW, SOC2 and network docs, benchmark script and test plan. we'll aim for the benchmark early next week pending David's staging details.
[04:51] Maya: quick technical note — for the benchmark we'll need sample traffic (json lines), a staging VPC peering, and SSH to your test harness for measurement.
[04:59] David: I'll get the traffic profile and peering IPs to you by Friday.
[05:04] Ethan: For the quality regression, we'll provide a 500 prompt eval set.
[05:08] Maya: Perfect. we'll run it across full precision and quantized variants and share token-level metrics.
[05:15] Jordan: Any other blockers?
[05:18] Priya: Not from engineering; just need to see the p99 numbers from the benchmark.
[05:22] Sara: Procurement will review the draft SOW and terms; we might ask for a one-time onboarding credit.
[05:27] Jordan: Ok we'll include onboarding credits in the sheet as options.
[05:31] Ethan: One more question — what's Redwood's process for fallbacks if a Dedicated pool gets overloaded?
[05:37] Maya: We have automated fallback policies — you can allow overflow to our hosted pools or to a lower-cost model variant. In Dedicated you can also configure burst nodes to absorb spikes.
[05:48] Ethan: Good.
[05:50] Jordan: Alright let's recap action items and dates.
[05:54] Maya: I'll send test plan and benchmark script by EOD tomorrow.
[05:58] Liam: I'll share SOC2 and network diagram link by Friday.
[06:02] Jordan: I'll send the pricing spreadsheet and draft SOW by Thursday.
[06:07] David: I'll provide traffic profile and peering details by Friday.
[06:12] Sara: Procurement will aim to review within a week after receiving the SOW.
[06:16] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark slot.
[06:20] Priya: Thanks.
[06:22] Ethan: Thanks all.
[06:24] Meeting end.
